proof_summary: Counting pairs divisible by each power of \(p\) gives the numerator valuation \(\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor^2\), while Legendre’s formula rewrites the denominator valuation in terms of the same floors; a termwise bound also establishes the required exact divisibility. Thus the quotient’s valuation depends only on \(\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor\) for \(i\ge1\), and these are unchanged when \(N=np\) is replaced by \(np+k\) with \(0\le k<p\).
